title: Parse a 32-Bit Signed Integer Problem

content.problemStatement:
Task: Convert string s to a signed 32-bit integer using these rules: discard leading spaces, read one optional sign, then consume consecutive decimal digits. Stop at the first non-digit. If no digits are read, output 0.

Clamp values below -2^31 to -2^31 and values above 2^31 - 1 to 2^31 - 1.
constraints: s contains only ASCII characters; typical inputs include letters, digits, spaces, '+', '-', and '.'.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: There are no leading spaces or sign characters to process. All digits form the value 42.
Leading spaces are ignored, then the minus sign is applied to the digits 42. The parsed result is -42.
The parser reads the consecutive leading digits 4193 and stops at the space before "with". Therefore the result is 4193.

hidden.label: Tab is not an ASCII space
Newline is not an ASCII space

notes: Only ASCII space (' ') is treated as leading whitespace.
Parsing stops immediately after the first non-digit character.
If no digits are parsed, return 0.
Overflow must be clamped to the signed 32-bit range.
Do not rely on built-in string-to-integer conversion routines.

solution.approach: Three-phase parse: skip leading whitespace, read optional sign, then accumulate digits while checking for overflow before each multiply/add. If overflow would occur, return the appropriate 32-bit bound. Use 32-bit accumulation and pre-checks to respect the 'no 64-bit arithmetic' constraint.

hints: Skip only the leading ASCII spaces before parsing.
Read at most one optional '+' or '-' sign immediately after the spaces.
Consume digits until the first non-digit character.
Before multiplying the current result by 10, check whether doing so would overflow a signed 32-bit integer.
Clamp the final answer to [-2147483648, 2147483647] if overflow occurs.
followUps: Can you solve the problem using only 32-bit integer arithmetic without using long/long long or BigInteger?
How would you modify the parser to support hexadecimal or binary numbers?
How would you extend the parser to support floating-point numbers?
learningObjectives: Handle whitespace and optional sign characters correctly.
Detect integer overflow before it occurs.
Use finite-state style parsing for structured input.
